script.title: Bonus Shares vs Rights Issue
script.caption_hook: Bonus shares are free, rights shares aren't. Here's the full difference.

lines.say: Bonus shares are free, rights shares aren't? Confusing, yaar!
Good question! Both go to existing shareholders in the same ratio as their holding. But one brings cash.
Bonus shares are free. Reserves become share capital. Rights shares are different: holders pay for them.
Wait, can I refuse a rights offer?
Yes. You can accept or renounce it. Nobody is forced.
And in the books, what happens for bonus?
For bonus, debit the reserve and credit Equity Share Capital. Money just moves inside equity.
Right. Reserves fall, capital rises equally. A rights issue increases equity.
Debit Bank, because cash comes in. Credit Equity Share Capital and Securities Premium.
Can any reserve fund a bonus?
No. Use free reserves, securities premium or capital redemption reserve. Revaluation reserve is not allowed.
Remember: bonus is a book entry only. Rights bring rupees into the bank.

check_notes: Checker: Line 12 (voice and board 'Rights issue entry'): the line says Securities Premium is always credited, but rights shares can be issued at par. Correct version: 'Debit Bank; credit Equity Share Capital, and credit Securities Premium only if the shares are issued at a premium.' On the board, mark the premium line '(if at premium)'.

Checker: Line 8 (voice): 'Money just moves inside equity' is loose, because no money moves in a bonus issue. Correct version: 'The amount just moves from reserves to share capital within equity; no cash is involved.'

Checker: Line 14 (voice and board 'Allowed for bonus'): under Section 63 of the Companies Act, 2013, securities premium can fund a bonus issue only if it was collected in cash, and reserves created by revaluation of assets cannot be used. Suggested wording: 'free reserves, securities premium collected in cash, or capital redemption reserve; revaluation reserve is not allowed.'
